newsitem.title: USA: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER ON EXPORT PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER ON EXPORT PROSPECTS.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on prospects for increased exports of U.S. wheat, traders said.
"There's talk about a lot of exports coming in but I haven't seen it, just bits and pieces here and there," said Tom Levis, analyst for Prudential Securities, "but the Egyptian business may come in."
There was talk Egypt late this week or over the weekend may buy 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat which would complete Egypt's September requirements, traders said.
Morocco this week set a retender for August 12 for 90,000 tonnes of optional original wheat and there was talk Pakistan soon may be in the market for wheat.
European traders said Iraq bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat.
U.S. wheat prices returned to competitive levels after a break earlier this week and the EU late last week imposed a tax on wheat exports which was underpinning wheat futures.
"People realized prices may have gotten too low so there was more talk about exports," Levis said.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 10 cents per bushel higher, with September up 8-3/4 at $3.62 a bushel.

Wheat futures dropped in early dealings on Tuesday in response to a Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above USDA's July forecast for 2.431 billion bushels.
But the market was recovering by Tuesday's close on the commercial buying.

A rebound in corn and soybean futures Wednesday tied to weather jitters also boosted the wheat market, traders said, as did expectations for USDA Tuesday to reduce its estimate for Canadian and Australian wheat production.
USDA at 0730 CDT Tuesday is slated to release its crop production and supply/demand reports.

Cargill Inc bought one million bushels each of September and December and sold one million December and sold one million March, traders said. Refco Inc bought two million September and bought 2.5 million December, traders said. LIT America sold 2.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, above the 23,050 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 400 December $3.90 calls at 13-1/2 cents and Smith Barney sold 500 December $3.60 puts at 12-1/2 cents, floor sources said.
Tenco Inc sold 250 December $3.60 puts at 12 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 10,975 traded Tuesday.
